create.name: Tibet House, New Delhi
create.bio:
Tibet House in New Delhi serves as the Dalai Lama's own cultural centre in India, and his outlook shapes its work: dialogue between cultures and faiths, conversation between science and Buddhist thought, and care for the planet seen through a Buddhist lens. Its collections began with the sacred objects and texts that Tibetan refugees carried into India after 1959, and the Dalai Lama laid the foundation stone of its present building on Lodhi Road in 1974.

The five-storey building holds a museum of Tibetan art, a library of manuscripts and books, a gallery, a conference hall and a bookshop. Led by its director, Geshe Dorji Damdul, Tibet House teaches the Nalanda tradition of Buddhist philosophy and practice through graded online courses, from an introductory level through certificate and diploma courses to a masters course, with interpretation into several languages, and it runs a Tibetan language course online and in person. Public lectures, conferences pairing Buddhism with science, residential retreats and ceremonies for Buddhist holy days fill out the year. Its YouTube channel records these teachings, retreats and lectures in English, Tibetan and other languages.

courses.title: Nalanda Certificate Course (Batch 4)
courses.description: A course of about 22 weeks in Buddhist philosophy and practice in the Nalanda tradition, taught online with English and Russian options and followed by a quiz. Registration opens on 10 December 2026; soft copies of the study material are included.
courses.price: Rs 1600 INR (non-monastics and non-students); Rs 400 INR for students; Rs 0 for monastics

courses.title: Indo-Tibetan Art and Culture Study Group membership
courses.description: A members' group, running since 1985, that meets monthly at Tibet House for talks by scholars on Tibetan and Buddhist subjects, with occasional film screenings. Members join by sending in a printed form.

free_resources.title: Resources: study and meditation manuals
free_resources.description: Downloadable study material from Tibet House, including an English study and meditation manual on bodhicitta and a Nalanda Buddhist philosophy text in Tibetan, English, Russian and Hebrew.
